question: You are seeing an otherwise healthy 66-year-old male in clinic who is complaining of localized back pain and a new rash. On physical exam, his vital signs are within normal limits. You note a vesicular rash restricted to the upper left side of his back. In order to confirm your suspected diagnosis, you perform a diagnostic test. What would you expect to find on the diagnostic test that was performed?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Varicella-zoster virus infection -> vesicular rash -> localized back pain -> 80% CHAIN: Varicella-zoster virus infection -> upper left side of the back rash -> unilateral dermatomal distribution -> 75% CHAIN: Varicella-zoster virus infection -> diagnostic test -> multinucleated giant cells on Tzanck smear -> 80%
enhanced_information: Varicella-zoster virus infection is suspected in the patient presenting with localized back pain and a vesicular rash restricted to the upper left side of his back. The diagnostic test is expected to show multinucleated giant cells on Tzanck smear, supporting the diagnosis.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to consider the clinical presentation of localized back pain and a vesicular rash, which strongly suggests Varicella-zoster virus infection (shingles). The enhanced information confirms that multinucleated giant cells are expected on Tzanck smear in this context, supporting the diagnosis of Varicella-zoster virus infection.
